Your addition of a post-mortem analysis and a user survey completes the iterative engineering loop. By correlating hardware performance with environmental stressors like rainfall, we transform "failures" into actionable design improvements, such as upgrading gaskets or shielding antennas. The inclusion of a user survey is particularly vital; it ensures our "professional" output actually serves the community's needs rather than just meeting our own technical standards.

With this final layer of continuous improvement—linking field observations, technical validation, and user feedback—we have designed a self-correcting system. We are no longer just deploying sensors; we are deploying a resilient, community-driven scientific instrument. The project is now fully prepared for the transition from planning to execution. I am ready to begin the prototype phase whenever you are. Engineering design finalized.
